title: Design Your First Agent: Production CRM Agent
subtitle: Hands-On Capstone: Design a multi-capability CRM agent that summarizes chats, drafts emails, books meetings, and escalates safely.

lessons.title: Design Your First Agent: Production CRM Agent
lessons.hook: You are tasked with deploying an autonomous enterprise CRM agent. It must handle high-volume customer inquiries: extracting key facts from messy conversations, drafting personalized emails, scheduling calendar invites, and recognizing high-risk situations (VIP cancellations or compliance threats) to escalate to human agents immediately. How do you assemble models, tools, instructions, and human oversight into a unified system?
lessons.bigIdea: Designing an autonomous agent is not about finding the biggest LLM; it is about architectural composition. You configure the Three Pillars (Reasoning Engine, Tool Schemas, Behavioral Compass), select an orchestration topology (ReAct vs Manager-Worker), and enforce concentric guardrails with Human-in-the-Loop escalation.
lessons.plainEnglish: Think of building a smart employee for your customer success team: you give them a brain (the model), a desk with tools (calendar, email, database), an employee handbook (instructions & limits), and a manager who steps in when high-stakes decisions arise.
objectives: Select the appropriate LLM reasoning tier based on latency and cost tradeoffs
Define 4 standard CRM tool schemas: Chat Summarizer, Email Drafter, Meeting Scheduler, and Safe Escalation
Formulate role-specific system instructions and operational boundary guardrails
Configure Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) approval gates for sensitive actions
Simulate live customer queries and evaluate agent behavior with the interactive AI coach

sections.title: The CRM Agent Design Challenge
sections.content: Enterprise CRM workflows are inherently multi-modal, stateful, and high-stakes. Customer interactions span unstructured chat transcripts, calendar coordination APIs, email dispatch protocols, and strict SLA compliance. A CRM agent must operate with speed on routine inquiries while never exceeding its authority on sensitive negotiations.

subsections.title: Session Guidelines
subsections.content:
• The AI coach helps you reflect. There are no scores or grades.
• Ask clarifying questions anytime. The session adjusts to your responses and learning style.
• Each session stays focused on the concept. You will receive structured feedback at the end of the session.

sections.title: The 4 Core Architectural Capabilities
sections.content: Our CRM agent integrates four modular capabilities through standardized tool interfaces:

subsections.title: 1. Chat Summarizer
subsections.content: Distills multi-turn support threads into structured bullet points, extracting customer sentiment, intent, and unresolved blockers.

subsections.title: 2. Contextual Email Drafter
subsections.content: Generates professional, personalized follow-up correspondence grounded in conversation history and verified company knowledge.

subsections.title: 3. Calendar Meeting Scheduler
subsections.content: Interacts with calendar availability APIs, validates timezones, checks conflict slots, and dispatches calendar invites.

subsections.title: 4. Safe Human Escalation (HITL)
subsections.content: Detects high-risk signals (churn threats, refund requests > $1,000, angry sentiment) and pauses execution for human review.

sections.title: Trade-offs: Autonomy vs Verification
sections.content: Granting total autonomy to send emails and schedule meetings without review risks erroneous bookings or brand damage. Conversely, requiring human sign-off on every routine summary creates catastrophic reviewer bottlenecks. Modern systems apply dynamic thresholding: full autonomy for reading and drafting, paired with gated approvals for external modifications.

subsections.title: Concentric Safety
subsections.content: Input guardrails sanitize prompts; tool preconditions verify authorization; HITL checkpoints intercept high-stakes operations.

quiz.question: When designing the CRM agent, which action should mandate a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) sign-off gate?
options: Generating an internal chat summary for the agent's short-term buffer
Issuing a full customer account cancellation with a $4,500 refund
Checking available calendar slots for tomorrow at 2 PM
Parsing customer text into structured JSON intent
quiz.correctAnswer: Issuing a full customer account cancellation with a $4,500 refund
quiz.explanation: High-stakes financial or irreversible operations (like issuing large refunds or cancelling accounts) require explicit human sign-off to prevent catastrophic errors.

recap: Designing production agents requires balancing model selection, tool definitions, and guiding instructions.
The CRM agent integrates 4 core tools: Summarizer, Email Drafter, Meeting Scheduler, and Safe Escalation.
Dynamic Human-in-the-Loop gates ensure safe execution without compromising day-to-day operational velocity.
The AI coach provides reflective guidance and diagnostic feedback to refine your agentic architecture.
